conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for coming in today. I’m Claire, a perinatal-mental-health clinician, and I’m here to help you settle into this new-mother chapter while keeping an eye on how you’re feeling emotionally. We’ll use a short, well-studied questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days; it isn’t a test of how well you’re parenting—just a quick way to see if you could use a little extra support right now.

Everything you share stays confidential within our team, and if at any point you need to pause, we will. When you’re ready, I’ll ask the questions conversationally—no forms to fill out—and we’ll go at your pace.

Shall we begin? Thinking back over the past week, how often have you found yourself able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not much. I’ve had maybe one or two moments where something made me crack a smile, but most of the time it feels like there’s this heavy cloud hanging over me. Even when my partner tries to joke around, I just can’t seem to find anything funny anymore.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often… maybe once or twice I’ve managed a little laugh, but mostly I feel like I’m just going through the motions.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but this week I haven’t really looked forward to anything. Even when my sister offered to come over so I could nap, it just felt like one more thing to survive, not enjoy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking it must be something I did—maybe I’m not reading his cues right or I’m just not cut out for this. Even when my partner says it’s normal, I still feel like I’m failing him somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

That happens almost every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart races because I’m sure he’s not breathing right, or I’ll lie awake convinced the stroller will tip over on our walk tomorrow. There’s no real reason—it’s like my brain invents scary “what-ifs” and won’t let go.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week. Once, I was just folding laundry and suddenly felt like I couldn’t breathe—my chest got tight, my hands shook, and I had to sit down. Nothing had happened; the baby was asleep, the apartment was quiet, but it felt like something awful was about to happen.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. Between the night feedings and the crying spells I can’t always soothe, it feels like I’m drowning in small tasks. I’ll start a bottle of pumped milk, realize I forgot to switch the laundry, then the baby spits up everywhere—it just piles up until I want to sit on the floor and cry.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… even when the baby finally dozes off, my mind keeps spinning. I lie there replaying everything I might’ve done wrong—did I burp him long enough, did I miss a rash, am I already ruining him? It takes me forever to fall asleep, and then I jerk awake at every tiny sound, heart pounding.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. There’s this heavy sadness that just sits on my chest the moment I open my eyes. I’ll be holding the baby and tears start rolling down my face for no clear reason. I keep telling myself I should feel grateful, but instead I just feel empty and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve ended up in tears three, maybe four times since last weekend. Once was when the baby wouldn’t latch—after twenty minutes I just broke down sobbing. Another time I was staring at a sink full of bottles and suddenly felt overwhelmed; I sat on the kitchen floor and cried while my partner tried to comfort me.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I feel low, but I’d never want to leave my baby without a mom.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note**

**Symptom Highlights**  
- Persistent low mood, daily tearfulness, marked anhedonia  
- Excessive self-blame and guilt regarding infant care  
- Recurrent, unprovoked anxiety, panic-type episodes (physical symptoms, catastrophic “what-ifs”)  
- Sleep disruption beyond infant demands (initial insomnia, hyper-arousal)  
- Frequent feeling “overwhelmed” and “drowning” in routine tasks  

**Pattern Summary**  
Patient endorses core affective, cognitive, and somatic features consistent with postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety. No self-harm ideation reported; protective toward infant.  

**Screening Significance / Risk Factors**  
Moderate–high likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode and comorbid anxiety disorder.  
Priority flags: mood-linked insomnia, daily crying spells, functional impairment, panic symptoms, absence of pleasure or anticipatory enjoyment.  

**Safety Statement**  
Denies suicidal or self-harm thoughts; no current safety concern identified.  

**Next Steps for Referral**  
Recommend comprehensive clinical assessment (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS) and possible referral to perinatal mental-health specialist for evaluation and treatment planning.
